The whole flock wheels in a vast slow spiral, dragons at every height circling one another, wings catching the light as the spiral turns.
The entire roost erupts into flight at once, hundreds of wings unfurling and beating in a thunderous explosion off the cliffs.
Hatchlings and juveniles tumble and play-fight among the watchful adults on the nesting ledges, little wings flapping clumsily.
The brood descends on the kill together, a churning mass of scaled bodies and snapping jaws tearing the carcass apart.
Dozens of dragons stream southward in a long undulating ribbon, the migration column stretching across the sky from horizon to horizon.
The whole brood plunges in a coordinated hunting dive, folding wings tight and dropping like stones toward the herd below.
Dragons pack the cliffside ledges, grooming one another, scales rasping against scales as long necks curl to reach difficult spots.
A sky-battle erupts above the peaks, bodies colliding and separating, flame and wings and screaming voices tangling in furious combat.
The brood circles the smoking volcano in a great loose wheel, riding the hot thermals upward in lazy, effortless rings.
Hundreds of dragons spread their wings to the morning sun, covering the hillside in a vast patchwork of membranes drinking the warmth.
The mob surges toward the intruder, a roiling wave of dragons converging from all directions in a cacophony of shrieks and fire.
Juveniles jostle and squabble along the roosting ledges, shoving for position, snapping at rivals, tails lashing in constant quarrelsome motion.
The brood calls together at dusk, hundreds of voices rising in overlapping resonant cries that roll across the valleys like thunder.
Older dragons corral a panicking fish-shoal from beneath, driving it upward as others strike from above in precise coordinated chaos.
The flock banks hard together in unison, every dragon tilting at the same moment, turning the whole mass like a single living thing.
Dragons pile together in the cave for warmth, a dense breathing heap of wings and tails and slowly blinking amber eyes.
The young ones race each other across the open sky, weaving and cutting past the elders who watch impassively from the thermals.
The brood settles onto the ice shelf together, claws scraping stone, bodies pressing flank to flank against the bitter polar wind.
A long column of dragons glides silently over the sleeping city, the whole procession passing without a wingbeat in uncanny quiet.
The adults form a loose ring around the hatchlings, a living wall of scales and lowered heads watching the treeline carefully.
Dragons leap from the clifftops one after another in rapid succession, a continuous cascade of bodies hurling themselves joyously into open air.
The brood hunkers low in unison as the storm breaks overhead, hundreds of wings folded tight and eyes slitted against the gale.
Rivals display against one another across the ridge, puffing flame, spreading wings to full span, each trying to loom larger than the next.
The whole flock glides down to the river at once, landing in a tremendous thrashing of wings and spray to drink together.
Dragons chase one another in looping aerial play above the sea cliffs, spiraling and diving and pulling up shrieking with what sounds like joy.
